title: Generation Time (Doubling Time)

references.label: General microbiology/quantitative methods references (ASM, FDA BAM)

summary: Generation time (or doubling time) is the time it takes a population of cells to double in number during exponential (log-phase) growth.
explanation: During the exponential phase of a bacterial growth curve, cell number increases geometrically: 1 → 2 → 4 → 8, and so on, each doubling taking approximately the same amount of time under constant conditions. Generation time is calculated from the number of generations (doublings) that occurred over a measured time interval — see the Generation Time Calculator and its underlying formula. It is species- and condition-specific (temperature, medium richness, oxygen availability, and growth phase all affect it), so a generation time measured under one set of conditions cannot be assumed to hold under different conditions.
commonMisconceptions: Treating generation time as a fixed property of a species rather than a value specific to the conditions it was measured under.
Assuming generation time stays constant throughout an entire growth curve — it is only approximately constant during the exponential phase, not during lag, stationary, or death phases.
